target_customer: Independent retailers buying wholesale and the brands selling to them
problem: Independent shops found products slowly and carried inventory risk, while small brands struggled to reach and finance retailers.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on wholesale orders, plus retailer net terms and capital

founders.name: Max Rhodes
prior_employers: Square (product lead for Square Capital and Square Cash, 2013 to 2016)
founders.background_notes: Tested the early product in retail shops with the founding designer. All four founders worked together at Square from 2013 to 2016 per Contrary Research (https://research.contrary.com/company/faire) and Lightspeed (https://lsvp.com/stories/the-secret-to-faires-success-think-global-shop-local/). No education found in opened sources.

founders.name: Daniele Perito
founders.role: Chief Data Officer (Contrary Research calls him former CDO)
prior_employers: Square (director of security and risk engineering)

founders.name: Jeff Kolovson
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Lightspeed's Faire story and Contrary Research; the YC page lists only three founders and VentureBeat 2018 names three.

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided marketplace with machine learning matching, payments and risk on net terms. Standard engineering with credit risk as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided liquidity of brands and retailers and financing terms made it harder to replicate. Shopify's Handshake and Tundra later faded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Shopify's Handshake wholesale product was reported retired in 2023 and Shopify was rumored in July 2026 to be in acquisition talks, unconfirmed.

market_need_then: No dated 2017 demand source was found. Company framing says independent retail faced decades old wholesale obstacles.

branding.name_origin: First called Indigo Fair. A 2021 interview with the founding designer says the team liked that Faire stayed close to Indigo Fair while celebrating the doers and makers.
branding.domain_note: Uses faire.com, acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark, brand pages published for sellers

branding.brand_signature: Faire as a celebration of independent makers

rebrands.why: Per founding designer interview, closer to the original while more celebratory of customers. Date comes from a weaker secondary site (February 2018).

branding.community_and_virality: Faire hosts brand pages and a seller blog on naming. No fan or meme evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Dominant wholesale marketplace brand for independent retail with hundreds of thousands of retailers, though no source credits the name itself for growth.

outcome_analysis: Faire built a wholesale marketplace for independent retail and rose to a 12.59 billion post-money valuation in May 2022. It cut 20 percent of staff in November 2023 and roughly 250 more later, then employees sold shares at 5.2 billion in November 2025. Fortune reported in November 2026 that it is eyeing an IPO, and acquisition talks with Shopify were rumored but unconfirmed.
notes: Company website pages (faire.com/news/about and news.faire.com/?p=18) returned HTTP 403 and were not worked around. Fourth co-founder Jeff Kolovson (COO) comes from Lightspeed and Contrary Research; the YC page and the 2018 VentureBeat article list three. Founder education was not found in any opened source, so it is null. Seed about $4M has no date or stage in the source (other). December 2018: TechCrunch reports $100M as a $40M Series B led by Lightspeed and a $60M Series C led by YC Continuity, valuation $535M from an unnamed source. Series E $170M at $2.5B (2020-10-27, Sequoia-led) is from the earlier record and a Forbes headline, whose page returned 403; Series F $260M at $7B 2021-06-10 from Business Wire. November 2021 Series G $400M at $12.4B from the Faire newsroom; May 2022 $416M extension at $12.59B from TechCrunch, whose amounts replace the unverified Forge figure. Shopify acquisition talks come from secondary outlets and are a rumor. No competitor source dated near 2017 was found; Handshake and Tundra statuses come from SEO blogs.
